item.description: A company built on affordable healthcare reports record subscribers and a widening loss, because every patient it helps on the cheap tier costs it money. The mission is working. The numbers agree it is working.

item.title: Cirrus Buys Back Shares Its Refounding Founder Keeps Selling, Both Sides Pleased
item.description: The software company laid off 7 percent of its staff in October, costing up to $75 million. Over the same year, it has bought back nearly $1 billion of its shares.

item.description: The newly merged media giant plans to cut $2.2 billion by flattening management layers and shrinking office footprints. It also mandated five-day in-office attendance.

item.description: The auto-parts supplier told its union it could not afford their demands. The same week it started permanent layoffs, its board approved a $60 million stock buyback and a record $46 million dividend.

item.title: Telecom Confident Its Own Shares Are Worth $19.45, No, Really, They Are
item.description: When the bidder's own stock at its own closing price is used to calculate the offer's value, and the market says the math is wrong, finance says the market is wrong.

item.title: $298 Million Refund Cashed by the Same People That Raised the Price

item.title: Fuel That Hauled the 2x4 to the Site Now Costs More Than the 2x4
item.description: The man building $3M condos is furious that a 2x4 costs eight bucks, and he is saying this while standing in a bathroom that costs more than a house.

item.title: Post Office Makes Its Temporary Surcharge Permanent, Then Adds More
item.description: The agency has clarified that 'temporary' refers to the period during which the charge is being collected, not the charge itself.

item.title: Landlord Cheers Tax Increase That His Tenants Will Pay
item.description: The man who owns forty units on Reading Road has never been happier about a piece of paper that will cost him money.
